title: Email Phishing Attacks
summary: Fraudulent emails designed to trick users into revealing sensitive information or downloading malware. Attackers impersonate legitimate companies to harvest credentials.

title: Credential Stuffing
summary: Attackers use leaked username/password pairs from data breaches to gain unauthorized access to other accounts. Users who reuse passwords are especially vulnerable.

title: Spear Phishing
summary: Targeted phishing attacks that use personalized information about the victim. Attackers research their targets on social media and public records.

title: Business Email Compromise (BEC)
summary: Attackers compromise or impersonate business email accounts to fraudulently request wire transfers or sensitive data. Often targets financial departments.
indicators: Requests to change wire transfer details

title: Malware Distribution
summary: Email attachments or links that distribute ransomware, trojans, or spyware. Often disguised as legitimate documents or software updates.

title: SMS Phishing (Smishing)
summary: Phishing attacks delivered via text messages. Often include links to fake login pages or malware. Increasingly targets mobile users.

title: Vishing (Voice Phishing)
summary: Phone-based social engineering attacks where attackers impersonate trusted entities to extract sensitive information or credentials.
indicators: Threats of account closure or penalties

title: Watering Hole Attack
summary: Attackers compromise websites frequently visited by a target group, infecting visitors with malware. Often targets industry-specific sites.

title: Whaling (Executive Phishing)
summary: Targeted phishing attacks against high-profile executives like CEOs and CFOs. Uses executive-specific language and requests.
indicators: References to board meetings or mergers

title: Fake Antivirus/Security Software
summary: Malicious applications that pose as legitimate security software. Trick users into installing them by displaying fake security alerts.
indicators: Requests to enter credit card info

title: Data Harvesting Websites
summary: Fake login pages and survey sites designed to collect personal information. Often target social media, banking, and email accounts.
indicators: URL slightly different from legitimate site

title: Typosquatting
summary: Attackers register domain names similar to legitimate companies (one letter off). Users who mistype URLs are directed to fake sites.
indicators: Website looks similar to real company

title: Baiting Attacks
summary: Attackers offer something enticing (free software, gift cards) to trick users into downloading malware or revealing information.
indicators: Too good to be true offers
Free software downloads from unknown sources

title: Pretexting
summary: Social engineering technique where attackers create a fabricated scenario to extract information. Often impersonates IT support or authority figures.
indicators: Claims to be from IT/Security team

title: Password Reset Scams
summary: Attackers trick users into using fake password reset links or provide incorrect password reset steps. Results in account compromise.
indicators: Links in unexpected password reset emails
Requests to confirm unusual login attempts

title: Dumpster Diving
summary: Attackers search trash for sensitive documents, passwords, or information that can be used to compromise accounts or physical security.

title: Shoulder Surfing
summary: Attackers watch over someone's shoulder to capture passwords, PINs, or sensitive information as they type or view screens.
indicators: Clear view of your screen from others

title: QR Code Phishing
summary: Fraudulent QR codes that direct users to phishing sites or malware. Often placed on posters, emails, or physical locations.
indicators: Poor print quality of QR code

title: Payment Redirect Scams
summary: Attackers intercept invoices and redirect payments to fraudulent accounts. Often sent via email after compromising accounts.
indicators: Invoice email from slightly wrong address
New payment instructions in old accounts

title: Website Cloning
summary: Attackers create exact copies of legitimate websites to harvest credentials and sensitive information from unsuspecting users.

title: Invoice Fraud
summary: Scammers send fake invoices to companies, requesting payment for services or products never provided. Exploits trust in vendor relationships.

title: Tech Support Scams
summary: Scammers pose as tech support to convince users to grant remote access or pay for fake software. Often targets inexperienced users.

title: Account Enumeration
summary: Attackers test if usernames or emails exist in a system. Used to identify valid accounts before launching further attacks.
indicators: Multiple login attempts with different passwords
Password reset requests for many emails

title: Social Media Impersonation
summary: Attackers create fake profiles impersonating individuals or companies to gain trust and trick victims into sharing information.

title: Romance Scams
summary: Scammers create fake romantic relationships to build trust and eventually request money or sensitive information from victims.
indicators: Requests for money or gift cards

title: Lottery/Prize Scams
summary: Scammers notify victims that they've won a prize or lottery they didn't enter. Request payment for taxes or fees to claim the prize.

title: Advance Fee Scams
summary: Scammers promise money, loans, or prizes but require upfront payment for processing fees, taxes, or verification. Disappear after receiving payment.

title: Nigerian Prince Scams (419 Fraud)
summary: Classic advance fee scam where scammers claim to have large sums of money requiring assistance to transfer. Victim pays upfront costs.

title: IRS/Tax Authority Scams
summary: Scammers impersonate tax authorities, threatening legal action or arrest. Demand immediate payment via gift cards or wire transfer.
indicators: Threats of arrest or legal action

title: Travel Booking Scams
summary: Fake travel websites offer deals that are too good to be true. Collect payment but never deliver the promised travel services.
